investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T07:01–07:08Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The pod's node affinity/selector further restricts scheduling to those same 2 nodes, leaving 0/6 nodes available. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never receives a running VM, the probe times out after 120–145 s, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes with no preemption victims available — this is the primary and most directly evidenced cause.

Node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, eliminating the other 4 nodes from consideration entirely and amplifying the capacity shortage.

No scale-out or node auto-provisioning triggered in time: preemption was attempted and found unhelpful, and no new node with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity became available within the 120–145 s timeout window.
Concurrent remote-agent workloads may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing the eval probe pods from being scheduled.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node output shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured to exclude all nodes (including the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a scheduling misconfiguration.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create is observed while the cluster node count and kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations remain unchanged, the failure may be transient or caused by a competing workload that has since released its slots.

If the eval runner itself failed before issuing the createAgent() call (e.g., auth failure, requireOrgId() error), the empty evidence object could have a different cause unrelated to pod scheduling — though the explicit Unschedulable scheduler message in the check output makes this unlikely.

If other non-remote-agent checks also failed at the same time with unrelated messages, a broader infrastructure or auth issue could be the true root cause rather than kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion specifically.
followUpEvals: Add a preflight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct warning before the pod scheduling timeout fires.
Add a kata.peerpods.io/vm headroom check that warns when fewer than N VM slots remain across eligible nodes, providing early signal before full exhaustion causes scheduling failures.
Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled separately from time-to-ready, so scheduling delays are distinguished from VM boot or runtime initialization delays.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that fires a single 'shared infrastructure failure' alert when all checks under remote-agents fail with the same Unschedulable message, reducing alert noise and making the shared root cause immediately visible.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T07:03–07:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the required peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements for remote agents. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod request is immediately placed in Unschedulable state. This prevents the eval runner from creating a remote agent, so the probe exits before writing any required evidence, producing a complete contract gap (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage, as no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 145s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=149972 endedAt=2026-07-09T07:05:36.175Z — the probe ran for ~150s before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, confirming the agent was never created and no state was polled.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial results were captured, consistent with failure before createAgent returned.
sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable message (120s timeout), confirming the scheduling failure precedes the state-polling step.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message (145s timeout), confirming the failure is not isolated to the state check.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905 (lines 1904-1905): the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent — if createAgent blocks on an unschedulable pod, no evidence is ever written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): requiredEvidence for remote-agent-state is [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — all missing because the agent pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint (e.g., a kata/peer-pod node selector) that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 are already at capacity. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were replaced/drained, the effective schedulable pool could have shrunk to zero even without resource exhaustion.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs failed to release resources from a prior run, those slots would remain occupied and block subsequent scheduling. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet, so this remains a hypothesis.

QUATERNARY — Cluster node count reduction: if one or more peer-pod-capable nodes were cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, the effective capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm would drop, causing new pods to be unschedulable. No node-event evidence is present in this packet.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule: if remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all fail with the same scheduler message within the same run window, automatically classify the failure as a shared infrastructure dependency failure rather than three independent check failures.

With no preemption victims available and preemption not helpful on the affinity-mismatched nodes, every new remote agent pod is left Unschedulable. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T07:01–07:08Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The pod's node affinity/selector further restricts scheduling to those same 2 nodes, leaving 0/6 nodes available. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the eligible nodes. As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never receives a running VM, the probe times out after 120–145 s, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, eliminating the other 4 nodes from consideration entirely and amplifying the capacity shortage.

No scale-out or node auto-provisioning triggered in time: preemption was attempted and found unhelpful, and no new node with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity became available within the 120–145 s timeout window.
Concurrent remote-agent workloads may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing the eval probe pods from being scheduled.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured to exclude all nodes (including the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a scheduling misconfiguration.

Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled separately from time-to-ready, so scheduling delays are distinguished from VM boot or runtime initialization delays.

Add a sibling-correlation eval that fires a single 'shared infrastructure failure' alert when all checks under remote-agents fail with the same Unschedulable message, reducing alert noise and making the shared root cause immediately visible.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T07:03–07:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the required peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements for remote agents. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod request is immediately placed in Unschedulable state. This prevents the eval runner from creating a remote agent, so the probe exits before writing any required evidence, producing a complete contract gap (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage, as no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 145s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=149972 endedAt=2026-07-09T07:05:36.175Z — the probe ran for ~150s before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, confirming the agent was never created and no state was polled.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message (145s timeout), confirming the failure is not isolated to the state check.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905 (lines 1904-1905): the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent — if createAgent blocks on an unschedulable pod, no evidence is ever written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): requiredEvidence for remote-agent-state is [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — all missing because the agent pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint (e.g., a kata/peer-pod node selector) that only 2 nodes carry, and those 2 are already at capacity. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were replaced/drained, the effective schedulable pool could have shrunk to zero even without resource exhaustion.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs failed to release resources from a prior run, those slots would remain occupied and block subsequent scheduling. No cleanup failure evidence is present in this packet, so this remains a hypothesis.

QUATERNARY — Cluster node count reduction: if one or more peer-pod-capable nodes were cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, the effective capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm would drop, causing new pods to be unschedulable. No node-event evidence is present in this packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote agent pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. With no preemption victims available and preemption not helpful on the affinity-mismatched nodes, every new remote agent pod is left Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 145s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler Unschedulable message after 120s, latencyMs=125094, evidenceKeys=[] — agent pod never scheduled, no evidence collected.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduler Unschedulable message after 145s, latencyMs=149972, evidenceKeys=[] — agent pod never scheduled, no evidence collected.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required contract fields absent (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) — consistent with the agent pod never reaching a running state.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151566, well below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 420000 defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a latency overrun.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — the agent creation step is the first blocking operation and it never completes when the pod cannot be scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the scheduling problem affects every remote agent pod attempt in this run.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or peer-pod VMs are consuming all available slots, leaving none for new eval pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes have a small vm slot quota, capacity is structurally limited regardless of current load.

Leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a prior eval run not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1916): if cleanup failed in a previous run, orphaned pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes.

Cluster node count or node pool scaling event: the eligible node pool may have scaled down or a node may be cordoned/drained, reducing effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed for a new eval pod.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and 4 affinity-mismatched nodes across all 6 cluster nodes, blocking every remote agent pod from starting (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, structurally limiting scheduling eligibility to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any vm slot exhaustion.

affectedAreas.reason: If prior eval runs left orphaned pods via a failed withCleanup (line 1916), those pods may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine whether slots are exhausted by active workloads or orphaned eval pods.
List all remote agent pods in the cluster and forcibly delete any that are stuck in Pending or that were created by prior eval runs and not cleaned up, to free vm slots.

Review the withCleanup implementation in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it handles failure paths (e.g., pod never scheduled) and does not leave orphaned pods that consume kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Assess whether the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods is intentional and whether the 2 eligible nodes have sufficient vm slot quota to support concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads.

If vm slot quota on the 2 eligible nodes is structurally insufficient, consider increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on those nodes, adding additional affinity-eligible nodes to the pool, or serializing eval runs to avoid concurrent slot contention.
Re-run all three remote-agents checks after remediation to confirm pods schedule successfully and all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are produced.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run a sibling local-agent check to isolate the failure to the remote scheduling layer
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: A passing local-agent check would confirm the failure is specific to the kata.peerpods.io/vm remote pod scheduling path and not a broader cluster or API issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: kubectl describe nodes showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (not exhausted) on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes would disprove the capacity exhaustion cause and point instead to a quota, admission, or configuration problem.

A successful re-run of any of the three remote-agents checks producing a scheduled pod would indicate the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly full node that has since freed slots) rather than a persistent capacity problem.

Evidence that the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are intentionally excluded by design and the 2 eligible nodes have sufficient vm quota would shift the diagnosis toward a transient load spike rather than a structural capacity deficit.
Presence of no orphaned or stuck remote agent pods in the cluster would rule out the leaked-pod / failed-cleanup hypothesis.

A passing run of local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime (which do not require kata.peerpods.io/vm) would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/peer-pod scheduling layer and not a broader cluster or API outage.
